I deleted my comment after doing more research into `React.lazy`: it uses `use()` logic for rendering lazily, so that is not the solution. There is a comment in `React.lazy` about refactoring to align the logic with `use()` better, so I do not think that is the cause/resolve of this issue. Updating `React.lazy` initialization should be done very carefully due to potential hidden dependencies on other runtimes (like react native). https://github.com/react/react/blob/e92ecef2806692f34e9d535da77405eb28464625/packages/react/src/ReactLazy.js#L123-L125 

Looking at the original reproduction of this issue, the problem is that `React.lazy` is being called in a component, causing it to be recreated at every render. As a result, `React.lazy's` internal promise state is not stored when we switch tabs. By default, suspense waits at least 300ms before rerendering to prevent too many screen changes,  


I updated my sandbox to see it https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/dcjmsz to have the in component (anti-pattern that the React docs warn against) 
https://react.dev/reference/react/lazy#my-lazy-components-state-gets-reset-unexpectedly


I opened an issue on react.dev to add a caveat about this: https://github.com/reactjs/react.dev/issues/8490.
